brief.headline: Earnings catalysts dominate a neutral tape; energy leads, tech diverges
brief.regime_summary: SPY sits 0.9% below its 20DMA and 5.0% above the 200DMA, down 0.4% on the week and 0.9% on the month. The regime is neutral, not trending. VIX at 19.68 is 18% above its own 20DMA of 16.72, signalling a volatility expansion that is not yet extreme but is meaningful. Sector breadth is thin: only 5 of 11 sectors hold above their 50DMAs. Energy (XLE +11.8% 20-day momentum) and defensives (XLU, XLP) lead; Technology (XLK -6.6%) and Communications (XLC -6.6%) are the clear laggards. In this backdrop, breakouts in beaten-down names carry less conviction, and earnings gaps will be the primary price discovery mechanism this week.

portfolio.note: Earnings Wednesday Oct 28. Price at $524.51, 0.4% below the 20DMA of $526.70 and 4.8% off the 20-day high of $551.15. RSI 52.6 is neutral; ATR is 2.2% so a one-standard-deviation move brackets roughly $513-$536 into the print. Five analyst revisions up, zero down in the last 30 days; EPS est +14.4% CY. Watch how the stock handles the 20DMA post-earnings.

Down 4.3% last week and 16.1% from its 20-day high; price at $1,571.80 sits 9.3% below the 20DMA and 10.0% below the 100DMA. RSI 35.2 approaches oversold. Fundamentals are intact (EPS revisions +7.5%, CY growth est +66.8%), but the MA stack is mixed and the tape is not buying semis right now. Thesis on duration of the drawdown warrants a fresh look.

Best-performing portfolio position on a momentum basis: 20-day mom +11.8%, 40-day +12.0%, RSI 69.8, only 0.6% below the 20-day high. XLE is the top-ranked sector. Position is working; trail a stop near one ATR (2.1%) below the 20DMA.

Down 4.0% last week; price at $366.61 sits 3.3% below the 20DMA and 5.8% below the 40DMA, RSI 34.1. The 40-day momentum is -13.3% and the MA stack is mixed. Gold futures (GC=F) at $4,025.90 show the same pattern. No news catalyst was found; the move appears macro/rate driven and the risk profile has changed materially from the entry.

watchlist.name: Accenture plc
watchlist.thesis: ACN gained 8.6% last week and is 17.2% above its 20DMA, 44.3% above the 100DMA. Revenue estimates have been revised up 5.3% in 30 days; 13 analyst upgrades vs 10 downgrades. Trailing P/E of 18.4 is 6% above its own historical median, which is modest given 20-day RS vs market of +44.2%. The move is extended but momentum is real. Next earnings Dec 17 removes near-term binary risk.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA $212.69, 20-day high $259.39, ATR-based stop ~1 ATR (4.0%) below entry
watchlist.risk: RSI at 73.2 and 69% 20-day realized vol mean any sector rotation back into XLK could see a sharp fade; the stock has moved far in a week on a neutral tape.

watchlist.name: Occidental Petroleum
watchlist.thesis: OXY is 7.0% above its 20DMA with RSI 68.6 and only 1.2% below the 20-day high. EPS revisions up 11.2% in 30 days; forward P/E 12.8 is 18.5% below its historical median, so valuation is supportive. Earnings Nov 9. Energy sector is the tape's strongest momentum group and crude oil remains above $100.
watchlist.risk: A reversal in crude below $95 would undermine the earnings revision story ahead of the Nov 9 print.

watchlist.name: Intuitive Surgical
watchlist.thesis: ISRG is 7.5% above its 20DMA, RSI 70.8, only 1.3% from its 20-day high. EPS revisions +4.4%, trailing P/E 54.7 is 28.6% below its own historical median. Healthcare sector holds above its 50DMA. Next earnings Jan 21, giving the setup room to develop without a near-term binary.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA $420.79 (implied from 7.5% gap), 20-day high $458.44 (implied), 1 ATR ~$13.20 (2.9%) stop distance
watchlist.risk: If the neutral regime deteriorates toward risk-off, high-multiple healthcare names tend to compress even when fundamentals are sound.

watchlist.name: ConocoPhillips
watchlist.thesis: COP is 10.5% above its 20DMA, RSI 76.8, 20-day mom +18.5%. EPS revisions up 7.1%; however trailing P/E of 19.97 is 51% above its historical median, the richest valuation flag in the screen. Earnings Nov 5 are the key gate.
watchlist.risk: RSI overbought at 76.8 and P/E well above history; a crude pullback or guidance miss on Nov 5 could unwind recent gains quickly.

watchlist.name: Bank of America
watchlist.thesis: BAC is in a full bearish MA stack, 13.4% below its 100DMA, RSI 26.4 (oversold but not bouncing). EPS estimates have been cut 4.4% in 30 days. 20-day momentum is -10.8%. Financials sector sits below its 50DMA. The oversold RSI creates bounce risk, but the trend and revision direction are both negative.
watchlist.levels: 20DMA $52.91 (implied from -4.4% gap), 20-day high $56.68 (implied), ATR 2.4% per day
watchlist.risk: An RSI this low can snap back sharply on any macro catalyst (Fed commentary, rates down); a close back above the 20DMA at ~$52.90 would break the short thesis.

watchlist.name: Intel Corporation
watchlist.thesis: Earnings Thursday Oct 29. INTC is 31.0% below its 20-day high, 16.5% below its 20DMA. RSI 32.8. 20-day momentum -29.3%. The stock is deep in a bearish MA stack and underperforming its sector by 22.7% over 20 days. Forward P/E 40.9 is elevated given no trailing earnings. A guidance miss or weak data center commentary could extend the break.
watchlist.risk: A positive earnings surprise into a deeply oversold RSI could produce a violent short-cover rally; position sizing should reflect the 6.5% ATR and binary event risk.

commodities.name: WTI Crude
commodities.note: At $101.13, WTI remains above the $100 level that has supported the energy sector thesis. Down 2.4% last week but 20-day momentum still +9.2%. The 8.5% pullback from the 20-day high and mixed DMA stack (above 20 and 40, trend unclear at 100) are worth watching as a signal for XLE and OXY.

commodities.name: Gold
commodities.note: Gold at $4,025.90 is 3.0% below its 20DMA, RSI 33.1. Down 3.2% last week with 40-day momentum at -11.1%. The GLD ETF mirrors this breakdown. Watch whether $4,000 holds as support; a failure would pressure the portfolio GLD position further.

commodities.name: Silver
commodities.note: Silver dropped 5.4% last week, the sharpest commodity decline in the screen. Bearish MA stack, RSI 30.6, 12.5% from 20-day high, and notably the relative volume printed 16.9x normal, suggesting a disorderly flush rather than steady distribution. Potential capitulation signal, but no bounce confirmation yet.

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.note: Natural gas at $3.02, essentially flat on 20-day momentum (+0.6%). Sits near its 20DMA with RSI 50.6, range-bound. High realized vol (65.6%) and thin liquidity mean entries are costly; watch for a directional break above $3.20 or below $2.80.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: Copper at $6.51 is flat versus its 20DMA (-0.6%), RSI 47.6, 20-day momentum -0.8%. Sideways action after heavy volume (6.8x normal) suggests the market is digesting a macro re-pricing. Copper's neutrality is consistent with the overall neutral regime signal.

risks: MSFT earnings Wednesday Oct 28: stock is just below its 20DMA at $524.51 vs $526.70; a miss or soft cloud guidance could break the bullish MA stack and pressure the broader XLK sector.

INTC earnings Thursday Oct 29: stock is 31% off its 20-day high with a 6.5% daily ATR. Binary risk is high and a negative print in a lagging sector could accelerate sector-wide selling in an already weak XLK.
VIX at 19.68 is 18% above its 20DMA of 16.72. Volatility is expanding without an extreme spike, a pattern that can persist and widen bid-ask spreads across the portfolio.

Gold and silver in simultaneous breakdowns (GC=F RSI 33.1, SI=F RSI 30.6, silver volume 16.9x normal) suggest a macro driver, potentially real rate or dollar strength, that could keep risk-off pressure on the portfolio GLD position.
Energy sector RSI (XLE 69.8, COP 76.8, OXY 68.6) is stretched. A reversal in crude oil from current $101 level would hit the portfolio's XLE holding and screen leaders OXY and COP simultaneously.

2026-11-09: OXY earnings (watchlist, EPS revisions +11.2% in 30 days)
